relevance_note: This single-centre cohort of 24 children with primary immunodeficiencies includes one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant: "Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency."
method_note: Read the full Markdown manually; no script transcribed any table (the script only assembled the JSON and checked spans). Scope decision: the paper describes 24 patients (plus a twin sister of Patient #13) with various primary immunodeficiencies; only Patient #18 has a TNFAIP3 variant, so only Patient #18 is extracted. The other 23 patients have no TNFAIP3 variant, and none is described as a relative of Patient #18. Label: 'Patient #18' (text) = '#18' (Table 2). Table 2 column 'A/S' = age at diagnosis (months)/sex per the table notes; age at diagnosis recorded as '192 (months)' and P192M, without converting units. Table 2 cells marked '-' for Physical findings and Additional manifestations are treated as not reported (rule 6), not as absence. 'without plasma cells' (histopathology) is recorded as a detail on the colitis and lymphonodular hyperplasia rows, not as its own feature. Pathogenicity: the authors call c.259C>T a 'mutation ... indicating an A20 deficiency' and list A20 deficiency as the final diagnosis, but give no formal classification, so the field is 'not reported'. No protein change, transcript, variant class, inheritance or parental testing is given. Lymphonodular hyperplasia (intestinal histology) was not mapped to the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' (left not reported); colitis/ileitis map to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; recurrent pulmonary infections map to 'recurrent infections'. Cohort-level counts (Tables 1 and 4, e.g. autoimmune manifestations 5/24) name no individuals, so they exclude nothing. No contradictions for Patient #18. Contradictions noticed for patients not extracted: Patient #12 'Whole-exome sequencing results were non-diagnostic' vs 'Whole exome sequencing was not performed'; Patient #17 gene 'NLRP1' in the text vs 'NRP1' in Table 2; Patient #23 is described as 'Sibling of patient #23'.
